plannedAlerts.alertTitle: Multiple failed logon attempts against SOC-FW-RDP

results.alertTitle: Multiple failed logon attempts against SOC-FW-RDP

summary.tpReason: The SecurityEvent table confirms 11,945 failed logon attempts (Event ID 4625) from a single source targeting 257 distinct accounts on SOC-FW-RDP between 10:43–11:43 UTC on Oct 26, 2021. This is a textbook brute force attack matching T1110.001. The volume and targeting pattern are consistent with automated password spraying against a publicly exposed RDP host.
summary.fpReason: No explanation for the 11,945 failed logons from a single source other than a brute force attack. The activity is not consistent with misconfigured services, legitimate password reset storms, or any benign pattern.
summary.whatHappened: Between 10:43 and 11:43 UTC on 2021-10-26, an attacker (source identifier: 41502da5-21b7-48ec-81c9-baeea8d7d669) conducted a brute force attack against SOC-FW-RDP, submitting 11,945 failed password attempts (Event ID 4625) targeting 257 different account names, including common defaults like ADMINISTRATOR, ADMIN, USER, TEST, and SERVER. All attempts failed. During the same window, 10 successful logons (Event ID 4624) were recorded, but all 10 were by NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM from the host itself using Negotiate authentication — routine OS service logons, not attacker activity. No user account was successfully authenticated. No successful logons from the attacker source occurred after the brute force window. No post-compromise activity (lateral movement, privilege escalation, or follow-up sessions) was detected on SOC-FW-RDP.
keyEvidence: 11,945 Event ID 4625 failures from single source (41502da5-21b7-48ec-81c9-baeea8d7d669) targeting 257 distinct accounts on SOC-FW-RDP, 10:43–11:43 UTC Oct 26 2021 — brute force confirmed
10 Event ID 4624 successes during alert window were ALL NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM local machine logons with Negotiate auth — not attacker-compromised user accounts
0 successful user account authentications during or after the brute force window — every password attempt failed
No follow-up activity (no lateral movement, no privilege escalation, no anomalous processes) detected on SOC-FW-RDP in the 24 hours after the alert
In the 24 hours prior to the alert, 0 Event ID 4624 logons were recorded on SOC-FW-RDP, indicating the SYSTEM logons during the alert are routine OS behavior, not anomalous
researchDone: Queried SecurityEvent table for all 4624/4625 events on SOC-FW-RDP during the alert window (10:43–11:43 UTC Oct 26 2021) to confirm brute force volume, account targeting, and check for any successful user logons
Queried SecurityEvent table for all 4624 events on SOC-FW-RDP in the 24 hours following the alert (11:43 UTC Oct 26 – 11:43 UTC Oct 27) to detect post-compromise activity — none found

Queried SecurityEvent table for 4624 events on SOC-FW-RDP in the 24 hours preceding the alert (Oct 25 10:00 – Oct 26 10:43 UTC) to establish baseline logon behavior — 0 logons recorded, confirming SYSTEM logons during alert are routine OS behavior
Examined SourceComputerId for the brute force source — all 11,945 failures originated from a single source identifier
